core.title: Migrate legacy artifact names to theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant
core.given: A plan artifact, an acceptance or another name carrier uses a legacy artifact name (no theme, or dots for hierarchy).
core.when: The planner migrates that name to the current scheme.
core.then: Rewrite it as theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant — assign a theme, colons between hierarchy levels, dots only before variants — and realign every name carrier from the profile (manifest, acceptance artifact, URN, contract file location and identity field) that carries it.
prefer: Steps in order: identify names -> determine theme -> identify hierarchy -> separate hierarchy from variants -> then update every name carrier from the profile, in the order the profile lists them (manifests, acceptance artifacts, URNs, contract file locations, identity fields).

Illustrative template shapes only, not a mandatory mapping table: a legacy name gains a theme; a dotted hierarchy becomes colon-separated; a dot survives only before a variant — any structurally valid migrated name satisfies the scheme.
avoid: Renaming only the name while any carrier — manifest, acceptance artifact, URN, contract layout or identity field — keeps the old one.
Dots between hierarchy levels, or a colon before a variant.
core.why: Piecemeal migration leaves URNs, manifests and contract identity fields pointing at different identities; one form with colons for hierarchy and dots for variants keeps them consistent.
evidence: Each migrated name has a theme prefix, colons only between hierarchy levels and dots only before variants.
No carrier from the profile — manifest, acceptance artifact, URN, contract path or identity field — still references the legacy name.
Contract files are reorganized to match the new hierarchy and their identity fields are updated consistently with the migrated identity.
verification: Needs two observers that the reference realization marks needs_new_observer: a detector that recognises legacy-shape names (no theme prefix, or dots between hierarchy levels), and a diff-level observer that sees such a name being rewritten in names, URNs and identity-field values.

The check validates each migrated name structurally — theme prefix, colons only between hierarchy levels, dots only before variants; the realization's reference mappings are illustrative examples, not a conformance table, so a different structurally valid migrated name is acceptable.
The check also verifies that no name carrier from the profile still references the legacy name, including contract file locations and identity fields.
Task-keyword and file-kind cues are contextual only and never raise a finding by themselves; a finding requires an actual legacy name being migrated.
A finding may cite individual steps of the ordered migration procedure; the step term and its enumeration are realization vocabulary.

values: name carrier (per profile: manifest, acceptance artifact, contract schema)
legacy artifact name in the pre-scheme shape (no theme prefix, or dots between hierarchy levels)
legacy name rewritten to the current scheme in names, URNs and identity-field values

fires: A plan artifact or task migrates a legacy artifact name (no theme prefix, or dots for hierarchy) to theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant.
A planner migrates a legacy artifact name and must update every carrier — manifests, acceptance artifacts, URNs, contract schema locations and identity fields — that carries it.
A legacy name with no theme prefix is found while authoring a new acceptance or other artifact and is to be migrated.
doesNotFire: Authoring a brand-new artifact name with no legacy predecessor (the naming-pattern rule governs that).
Renaming an artifact whose name is already in theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant form (an ordinary rename, not a migration from the legacy shape).
Editing a contract or manifest whose names are already in the current form and are not being renamed.
A task that merely mentions migration keywords or touches manifests, acceptance files or contracts without any legacy name being migrated.

profileRequirements.meaning: The artifact kinds, locations and identity fields that carry an artifact name, so that a migration must realign all of them, in a known order.
profileRequirements.bunValue: wagon manifest, feature file, URN, contract file location and $id field

proposedKeys.meaning: The artifact kinds, locations and identity fields that carry an artifact name (names, URNs, schema identity fields), which a name change or migration must realign together.
proposedKeys.bunValue: wagon manifest, feature file, URN, contract file location and $id field
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group defines per-artifact URN shapes, bindings and the plan-artifact declaration, but no key lists the cross-artifact carriers of a name — manifests, acceptance files, contract file locations and identity fields — that a migration must realign in order. roles.<role>.kinds maps roles to file kinds but cannot express URNs, identity-field names, or a wagon manifest, which plays none of the listed roles.

neutralityNotes: The core keeps the artifact-naming scheme itself — theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant, colons for hierarchy, dots for variants, and the v1/v2 scheme-version labels — because that is convention content, not stack machinery; the legacy (v1) shape is always defined structurally (no theme prefix, or dots between hierarchy levels). No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. The legacy-to-current reference mappings are strictly illustrative: the core neither requires reusing them nor validates against them as a table — verification checks naming structure and carrier consistency only, so a different structurally valid migrated name passes. What stayed realization-side: the concrete legacy reference mappings (Bun-corpus names), the finding/change/term ids of this rule's observers, and the concrete carrier kinds (wagon manifest, feature file, contract $id), which reach the core only through the proposed profile key urn.name_carriers. 'Contract schema' and 'identity field' are used as ATDD-concept-level terms that each stack binds via the profile.
